messages:
Jessica: Customer (acme) reporting intermittent partial SSE payloads after connection reconnects. They see duplicated 'data:' events and sometimes the final token is truncated. Uploaded pcap and logs. High priority—billing impact.
O'Brien: can you paste a minimal repro + client headers? hypothesize proxy/chunking.
Jessica: Client: mobile-sdk v1.4.2 using fetch polyfill + EventSource fallback. Reconnect loop: retry every 2s with resume_token. Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, Accept: text/event-stream, X-Client: acme-mobile
Sam: Which edge region? trace id?
Jessica: trace: trace-0a1b2c, edge: eu-west-1-edge-23. Server logs show upstream reset then immediate resume send. excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:01:22Z] conn id=abcd proxy: upstream reset
[2026-03-10T14:01:23Z] handler: resume token ok, resuming stream for client acme-user-12
[2026-03-10T14:01:23Z] send chunk: "data: {\"text\": \"hello\"}

"
[2026-03-10T14:01:24Z] send chunk: "
"
[2026-03-10T14:01:24Z] send chunk: "data: {\"text\": \"world\"}
"  <-- missing trailing 

```
Maria: That missing event delimiter (final CRLF) will make parsers treat it as an incomplete event. polyfills are picky about LF vs CRLF.
Jessica: PCAP uploaded to ticket: s3://redwood-support/acme/pcaps/2245678901.pcap. Repro attached: curl + eventsource polyfill steps.
Sam: share repro steps here so I can run locally. also include server write boundaries if possible (we need to know syscall frame boundaries).
Jessica: repro: 1) curl -N --header 'Accept: text/event-stream' "https://api.redwood.example/stream?resume_token=xyz" 2) trigger model response in 2 partial chunks (server sends first chunk, then connection reset) 3) client reconnects with same resume_token 4) client sometimes merges the end of the first chunk with the start of the second, and sometimes receives duplicates.
O'Brien: sounds like NGINX/edge write coalescing combined with our proxy not flushing explicit delimiters. writev can coalesce multiple writes into single TCP segment. If reconnect happens mid-segment the replay/resume logic can replay a partial frame and cause duplicates. we ran into similar with chunked transfer encoding flags.
infra-bot: note: deploy 2026-03-09T22:47:00Z touched proxy chunk buffer behavior on eu-west-1-edge-23 (commit: b7f4c3d).
Sam: plan:
- get tcpdump/tcpflow of the session and compare pcap frame boundaries to server write calls
- check proxy commit/flags on edge-23 and rollback candidate
- add temporary per-connection chunk-flush flag for acme so every logical event gets its own flush
- instrument runtime to emit per-event seq id header (x-rw-eid) so we can detect duplicate/overlap on resume
Maria: also test client polyfill: some EventSource shims treat single LF as delimiter, others require CRLF. Add tests that send final token with only LF and with CRLF.
Jessica: customer wants timeline + workaround asap. They can toggle any edge flags?
O'Brien: ops can toggle per-connection chunk-flush on edge-23 as mitigation. Not ideal long term.
Sam: I'll pull the pcap now and run tcpflow to verify whether the kernel coalesced small writes. If write syscalls show "data1

" then "data2
" but pcap shows them merged, we confirm writev/coalescing.
Maria: If confirmed, next steps: either force explicit flush after each event at runtime, or ensure proxy preserves flush boundaries (prefer latter). Also add an automated test in eng-runtime that simulates mid-segment reconnects.
Jessica: I'll ask customer to try the edge flag toggle and report back. attaching customer ticket link and requesting permission to run additional tests against their resumable token.
Sam: grabbing pcap and logs now. tagging @Maria and @O'Brien for runtime/proxy changes.
O'Brien: FYI we should also verify resume token TTL handling — if token replay happens, duplicate events could be caused by both client replay and server resend. Add server-side idempotency using x-rw-eid to dedupe on resume.
Jessica: thanks all. will update ticket when customer tries toggle. :thumbsup:
